&api-questions;
The nbfx Wizard API defines the JavaFX wizard SPI — Wizard and WizardPanel — the @WizardRegistration annotation and its processor, the metadata-only discovery contract WizardEntry/WizardRegistry, and the WizardDisplayer seam implemented by platform.wizard.
A module implements Wizard/WizardPanel and declares it with @WizardRegistration. The processor writes the id, display name, icon, category and position to NbFx/Wizards/<id>.instance; WizardRegistry.discover reads that metadata without creating the wizards, and WizardRegistry.find creates a fresh wizard when it is opened. The themed WizardDialog in platform.wizard is the T0 implementation that shows the pages; it registers itself as the WizardDisplayer service.
A downstream module implements a wizard with API imports only; the shell lists the registered metadata through WizardRegistry, creates the selected wizard through find, and shows it through WizardDisplayer. Each open starts with a fresh wizard instance, so no input is carried from a previous open.
WizardRegistryTest covers the layer metadata, ordering, fallback and that find creates only the requested wizard and returns a fresh instance each time. WizardRegistrationProcessorTest covers the generated layer fragment, a bundle reference for the display name, and the rejection of a class that does not implement Wizard. LayerInstancesTest covers the node-free reader and its warning for broken registrations, and AppShellConformanceTest exercises the registry and displayer on the platform-only classpath. The API is under development until the MVP freeze, after which API signature tests (sigtest) are enabled.
A JDK is required to compile the annotation processor, and a JavaFX runtime is required for WizardPanel and the themed dialog.
Only org.netbeans.api.nbfx.wizard is public. The processor implementation is an implementation detail and is not exported.
The processor is discovered by the compiler through the META-INF/services/javax.annotation.processing.Processor service, generated by @ServiceProvider(service=Processor.class). WizardDisplayer.getDefault finds the platform displayer in the default lookup, and WizardRegistry reads NbFx/Wizards from the configuration filesystem.
platform.wizard registers its WizardDisplayer implementation with @ServiceProvider; this module registers its annotation processor in the same way.
Yes. The processor creates NbFx/Wizards/<id>.instance entries.
WizardRegistry reads NbFx/Wizards through LayerInstances; discovery reads the metadata only and creates the wizard on demand.
None.
The annotation processor runs in the compiler's processing rounds and is stateless. WizardRegistry.discover reads metadata and may run on any thread; find constructs the wizard, and WizardDisplayer.show, Wizard.getPages, WizardPanel.getComponent and Wizard.finish run on the JavaFX Application Thread.
No code runs on startup; the module contributes a compiled annotation processor, and discovery happens on demand.
No code runs on exit.
No special requirements.
